name: Dentinogenesis Imperfecta Type 3

ethnicAssociations: Predominantly reported in individuals of Brandywine, Maryland descent

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Dentinogenesis Imperfecta

criteria.description: Teeth exhibiting opalescent, translucent, amber to blue-gray discoloration
Radiographic evidence of 'shell teeth' characterized by thin dentin and enlarged pulp chambers
Rapid attrition and enamel fracturing leading to early tooth loss
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of mutations in the DSPP gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of opalescent teeth with characteristic radiographic shell teeth and rapid dental wear
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical and radiographic findings are primary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Opalescent, translucent amber to blue-gray discoloration of teeth
Radiographic 'shell teeth' with thin dentin and enlarged pulp chambers
searchTerms: teeth with thin dentin and large pulp chambers
enlarged tooth pulp with thin dentin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapid attrition and enamel fracturing leading to early tooth loss
searchTerms: fast tooth wear and enamel cracking
early tooth loss from enamel breakage
teeth with bulbous crowns and narrow neck
permanent teeth with pulp filled in

common.symptomName: Increased tooth sensitivity to thermal stimuli
searchTerms: teeth sensitive to hot and cold

occasional.symptomName: Malocclusion due to abnormal tooth morphology
searchTerms: bad bite due to tooth shape

occasional.symptomName: Increased risk of dental abscesses without caries
Mild gingival inflammation secondary to dental abnormalities
searchTerms: mild gingivitis due to tooth issues
gum swelling related to dental abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss associated with DSPP mutations
rare.notes: Reported in some cases but not consistent
searchTerms: hearing loss linked to gene mutations

rare.symptomName: Bone abnormalities such as mild osteopenia
Temporomandibular joint dysfunction secondary to malocclusion
searchTerms: jaw joint pain from bite problems
TMJ dysfunction due to misaligned teeth

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing mutations in DSPP gene
imaging: Panoramic and periapical dental radiographs showing shell teeth with thin dentin and enlarged pulp chambers
Cone-beam CT may demonstrate detailed tooth morphology abnormalities
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in DSPP (dentin sialophosphoprotein) gene
other: Clinical dental examination revealing opalescent teeth with rapid wear

distinguishingFeatures: Similar dental findings without bone fragility
Absence of shell teeth radiographic pattern
Primarily enamel defects rather than dentin

redFlags: Early and rapid tooth loss in childhood
Severe enamel fracturing with minimal trauma
Radiographic evidence of shell teeth with enlarged pulp chambers
references: Wang S, et al. Dentinogenesis imperfecta type III: clinical, radiographic, and genetic analysis. Oral Dis. 2019;25(7):1763-1770.
Kim JW, Simmer JP. Hereditary dentin defects. J Dent Res. 2007;86(5):392-399.
